questions.question: Which one of the following is an example of physical equilibrium?
questions.explanation: Physical equilibrium involves only changes of physical state (e.g., phase changes). “Solid ⇌ Liquid” is purely a phase change, unlike the other listed chemical reactions.

questions.question: Match the following equilibria with the corresponding condition. List-I List-II A Liquid ⇌ vapour 1 Saturated solution B Solid ⇌ Liquid 2 Boiling point C Solid ⇌Vapour 3 Sublimation point D Solute (s) ⇌ solute (solution) 4 Melting point 5 Unsaturated solution
questions.explanation: (I) Liquid ⇌ Vapour → Boiling point. (II) Solid ⇌ Liquid → Melting point. (III) Solid ⇌ Vapour → Sublimation point. (IV) Solute(s) ⇌ Solute(solution) → Saturated solution.

questions.question: A chemical reaction is at equilibrium when
options: Equal amounts of reactants and products are present
Reactants are completely transformed into products
Rates of forward and backward reactions are equal
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, a reaction’s forward and reverse rates balance each other exactly, so there’s no net change in concentrations. This does not require having equal amounts of reactants and products, nor does it mean minimal product formation or complete conversion of reactants. The key criterion is that both reaction directions occur at the same rate.

questions.question: Which of the following graph correctly represents a relation between rate of reaction w.r.t. time ?
questions.explanation: In the reversible reaction. At the initial time of the reaction the forward reaction rate is at maximum while backward reaction rate is zero. After some time as the reactants start to convert into products rate of forward reaction starts to decrease and backward reaction rate starts to increase. At the time of the equilibrium both forward and backward rate of reaction becomes equal to same and remains like this.

questions.question: In chemical reaction A B , the system will be known in equilibrium when:
options: The rate of change of A to B and B to A on both the sides are same
questions.explanation: At dynamic equilibrium, concentrations become constant because the two opposing reaction rates are equal, not because reactants are fully consumed or a fixed percentage has reacted (NCERT Class 11, Unit 7 “Equilibrium”).

If Assertion (A) is True but the Reason (R) is False.

questions.question: 1 mole of {A}({g}) is heated to 2000^{} {C} in a 1 litre closed flask, till the following equilibrium is reached, {A}({g}) {B}({g}) . The rate of forward reaction at equilibrium is 0.02 {~mol} {lit}^{-1} {~min}^{-1} . What is the rate ({mol}. . Lit .{ }^{-1} {~min}^{-1}) of the backward reaction at equilibrium?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the backward reaction. Since the forward‐reaction rate at equilibrium is given as 0.02 mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹, the backward‐reaction rate must also be 0.02 mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹.

questions.question: The following statement is incorrect about chemical equilibrium:
options: There is no change in the concentrations of reactants and products with time
Equilibrium can be attained by starting with either reactants or products
Position of equilibrium cannot be disturbed by changing the concentrations of reactants or products
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants/products remain constant over time (statement A is correct). Equilibrium can be reached starting from reactants or products (B is correct). It is dynamic, with forward and reverse rates equal (C is correct). Changing concentrations does shift equilibrium (Le Chatelier’s principle), so D is incorrect.

questions.question: Chemical equilibrium is dynamic because:
options: The concentration of the reactants and products become same at equilibrium
The concentration of reactants and products are not constant but different
Both forward and backward reactions occur at all time with the same speed
questions.explanation: Chemical equilibrium is dynamic because even though overall concentrations remain constant, the forward and reverse reactions continue happening simultaneously at the same rate, balancing each other out. This ongoing activity at the molecular level is why the system is called “dynamic,” rather than static.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a general characteristic of equilibrium involving physical processes?
options: Equilibrium is possible only in a closed system at a given temperature.
The equilibrium is dynamic in nature.
Measurable properties of the system keep changing.
Equilibrium can be attained from both sides of the reaction.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, measurable (macroscopic) properties such as temperature, pressure, and concentrations remain constant, even though the system is still dynamic at the molecular level.

questions.question: A reaction reaches a state of equilibrium only when:
options: The reactants and products stop reacting
The concentration of reactants and products become equal
The products react together at the same rate at which they are formed
All the reactants and products are in the same state of matter
questions.explanation: A system at equilibrium is characterized by the forward and reverse reactions occurring at equal rates. This does not necessarily require equal concentrations of reactants and products or the same phase; rather, no net change in composition occurs because the rate of product formation equals the rate of reactant formation.
